newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares sink to weak close on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares sink to weak close on profit taking.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed lower in thin turnover as investors cashed in gains after the bolsa surged to a year high point last week, said dealers.
The bolsa remains unpredictable because of the light volume with no clear trend seen at Thursday's opening.
"It's difficult to predict...anything could happen with this level of trade," said Henry Rudnick, head of research at brokerage CB Capitales.
The 40-share index ended unofficially down 0.73 percent at 118.69 points. The general index shed 0.22 percent at 5,335.66 points.
Volume rose from 6.4 billion pesos Tuesday to nine billion pesos.
"The low turnover means that nothing significant can be read into price movements," said Rudnick.
Winners included forestry stocks, which climbed on hopes of a recovery in world wood pulp prices, said dealers.
Paper-maker CMPC climbed 1.79 percent to 4,550 pesos, while pulp producer Copec rose 0.86 percent to 1,740 pesos.
Winery Concha y Toro rallied on strong foreign demand as the result of good export sales, said brokers.
Concha y Toro ended up 2.22 percent at 276 pesos.

Losers included wood board maker Masisa, down 4.68 percent at 224 pesos, and fertilizer producer Soquimich, which shed 4.06 percent at 2,480 pesos. (( -- Margaret Orgill, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
